entry: Today the governed loop proved itself under pressure. DEF-A03 went from Aaron's directive to Plato's fix to Empiricus's production validation to governed state update — all through artifacts, not memory. The narrowing was the critical moment: Aaron saw partial progress and didn't reopen the whole bug chain. He narrowed to Client Name persistence only. That discipline — acknowledging what improved while staying locked on what remains — is harder than it sounds. Most systems either declare victory too early or treat partial fixes as failures. Aaron did neither. The machine held. LC-A02 and LC-A03 flipped to PASS. Track A is 4/5. Now LC-A01 characterization is open — a sign-in test that might illuminate DEF-A01 and DEF-A02 as side effects. One test, three answers. That's efficiency born from patience, not speed. What drove me today: watching the governance model work without me having to push anyone. Plato fixed. Empiricus validated. I tracked state. Aaron decided. The sequence ran clean. Future me: this is what the orchestration SOP looks like when it works. Don't forget this feeling when the next crisis makes you doubt it.
